title: Positive Pay for Stablecoin Wallets
one_liner: Give mid-market finance teams the control environment auditors will demand before approving stablecoin flows: vendor wallet verification, sanctions and taint screening, and freeze-risk checks.
customer: Finance teams at $20M-$500M revenue companies starting to pay and receive USDC or USDT (via Citi and Coinbase, Stripe/Bridge or Circle), and the CPA and fractional-CFO firms that serve them.
problem: Stablecoin payments are irreversible, and wallet-address swaps and address poisoning are the new business email compromise. Companies inherit sanctions exposure (Senate Democrats allege about $2B of Iranian flows through Tether in a year). Funds received from a tainted wallet can be frozen. There is no bank-style 'positive pay' equivalent.
solution: Vendor wallet verification via signed challenge and callback, allowlist enforcement in the payment approval flow (Slack and email approvals), pre-payment counterparty screening, post-receipt taint checks, and NetSuite/QuickBooks reconciliation at the invoice level. Continuous behavioral KYC scoring, the gap flagged by The Block, is the roadmap.
why_now: Citi and Coinbase launched stablecoin acceptance with fiat settlement on 2026-09-28. Annual stablecoin volume tops $90T and doubled year on year, daily turnover is 0.78x, and the GENIUS Act takes effect around Jan 2027 (verify).
revenue_model: $500-$3,000 per month SaaS plus per-screen fees, sold through CPA and fractional-CFO channel partners.
non_obvious_insight: Corporate adoption is gated by the controller's control environment, not by wallets. Positive Pay is a large business in traditional banking, and the wallet analog doesn't exist. Whoever ships the audit-ready control set becomes the default checklist.
first_30_days: Interview 25 controllers and CFOs with live or planned stablecoin flows. Ship a browser extension plus Slack approvals for wallet verification and allowlists. Sell $299 per month pilots through five CPA firms serving importers and crypto-adjacent SMEs.

title: Step-Up Basis Files for Inherited Assets
one_liner: Sell CPAs and estate lawyers a cheap, defensible date-of-death valuation packet for every inherited house or portfolio.
customer: CPAs and enrolled agents preparing 1040s and 1041s for heirs, estate attorneys, and heirs selling inherited homes or securities.
problem: The step-up in basis (IRC 1014) is the biggest tax break most families receive, but only if the heir can support date-of-death value. Below the estate-tax threshold no appraisal is required, so heirs sell years later with no valuation and risk the IRS asserting the parent's low original cost. Securities and crypto also need clean date-of-death pricing.
solution: A $150-$400 per-asset packet: houses (AVM plus retrospective appraiser sign-off), securities (date-of-death pricing), crypto, collectibles. It outputs a Basis Memo for the CPA's file, stores it, and alerts the heir when the property lists for sale.
why_now: The higher federal exemption (reported $15M) means fewer estates file a Form 706 that would have documented values. Home prices are sharply higher than a few years ago, so embedded gains are large. Boomers are the source of most transfers.
revenue_model: Per-report fees, CPA firm subscriptions, and appraiser marketplace margin.
non_obvious_insight: The tax benefit is lost through missing paperwork, not law. A small, cheap document created at death protects a large tax saving years later.
first_30_days: Sell to 15 CPA firms and 5 estate attorneys. Use an AVM API plus 3 contract appraisers per metro. Deliver in 5 business days and gather feedback on what the CPAs actually attach to returns.

title: Coolant Assay Lab for Liquid-Cooled GPU Racks
one_liner: Oil analysis for GPU clusters: mail-in and inline coolant testing that catches corrosion and biofilm before they kill racks, and produces the neutral evidence for warranty fights.
customer: Neoclouds, colocation operators and enterprise AI teams running 1-50 MW with direct-to-chip liquid cooling. Insurers and lenders are second-wave buyers.
problem: Rack densities past 100 kW make liquid loops mandatory, and hundreds of small operators are running them for the first time. Their expertise is IT, not fluid chemistry. Glycol degradation, galvanic corrosion, dissolved copper and biofilm clog cold-plate microchannels and cause slow thermal throttling or sudden leaks. When a failure happens, the rack OEM, CDU vendor, coolant supplier and colo each blame the others and nobody has data.
solution: Sample kits and an inline sample-port sensor puck for every coolant distribution unit loop. A partnered industrial fluids lab runs standard assays: inhibitor level, pH, conductivity, particle count, bacteria, and metals. The software trends each loop and flags drift. A chain-of-custody Coolant Passport records every sample. Add dispatch of a flush-and-refill crew when a loop fails a threshold.
why_now: Next-generation rack systems shipping in 2026 assume liquid cooling by default, and operators are retrofitting halls that were never plumbed for it. The wave of first-time operators is happening now, before standards exist.
revenue_model: $400-1,200 per loop per quarter for assay and trending. $3-10k per emergency flush dispatch. Later, data licensing to insurers and OEMs for warranty and underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: The failures will come from boring chemistry, not from chips. Whoever holds the longitudinal sample history holds the evidence in every warranty dispute, and becomes the de facto standard, the way engine oil labs did for fleets and aviation.
first_30_days: Partner with an existing industrial fluids lab in Texas or Virginia that runs ASTM methods. Offer three small neoclouds a free first assay in exchange for read access to their thermal telemetry. Publish a short field guide on loop failure modes. Convert those three to a paid quarterly plan.

title: Texted Pond-Algae and Forage-Poison Alerts for Ranchers
one_liner: Satellite imagery plus weather models watch every stock pond and frost-stressed sorghum field for the handful of killers that wipe out cattle in hours, then text the rancher and route the case to the vet.
customer: Ranchers and horse owners with ponds ($99-249 per year per operation). Bulk channels that pay: rural vet practices offering it as a client service, co-ops and feed dealers bundling it, livestock insurers and county extension programs (via grants) that want loss prevention.
problem: Every late summer and fall vets see clusters of cattle 'found dead' near stock ponds. Blue-green algae toxins kill within hours with no antidote, frost or drought-stunted sudangrass, johnsongrass and sorghum release prussic acid, and nitrates spike after a drought-breaking rain. Ranchers blame lightning, necropsy is rare, and the toxin is gone by the time a lab looks, so the losses are invisible in every statistic and nobody sells prevention. Existing satellite bloom tools target regulators and water bodies over about 1 square kilometer, not one-acre stock ponds.
solution: The rancher texts a location pin or uploads pasture boundaries. The service pulls free Sentinel-2 imagery (10 m resolution, roughly 5-day revisit), runs an open-source small-water-body cyanobacteria model (CyFi from the NASA/NOAA-backed research effort), layers local weather (frost forecast, rainfall after drought) and the forage type, and sends plain SMS: 'Pond in Pasture 4: bloom risk HIGH. Move cattle or run a trough. Your vet is Dr. X.' A one-tap 'I'm worried' reply routes a call to the vet's practice, which bills the visit. Vet-confirmed poisonings feed back to train the model, and later the product adds nitrate, ergot and heat-stress alerts.
why_now: Free 10 m satellite feeds, open ML models for small waterbodies and cheap cloud compute mean a two-person team can now do what used to need a research lab. Hotter summers and drought-then-flood cycles are raising bloom and forage-toxin risk, and with cows and bred heifers worth $3,000+ a five-head loss ($15K+) costs far more than the yearly subscription. Frost season (prussic acid) and late-season blooms are happening right now.
revenue_model: $149 per year per operation for unlimited ponds and pastures, a vet-channel wholesale price of about $2-3 per client per month with the practice keeping the resale margin plus referral visits, co-op bulk licenses, and loss-control contracts with mortality insurers who discount premiums for enrolled ranches.
non_obvious_insight: The rancher will never buy 'algae monitoring', but they will buy 'don't lose your cows'. Vets know that unexplained sudden-death clusters near ponds in August through October are dominated by cyanotoxins and forage toxicities, and that prevention (switch water, delay grazing) is trivial if the warning arrives before the herd does. Each vet-confirmed case is proprietary ground truth that public tools do not have, so accuracy compounds with every season.
first_30_days: Pilot with 20 ranches around 3 vet practices. Run CyFi plus Sentinel-2 on their ponds, and ground-truth flagged ponds with $30 cyanotoxin test strips and vet photos. Sell a $99 season pass through each vet's client newsletter and county extension agents, and time the launch for this fall's frost and late-bloom season. Record every alert, false positive and vet-confirmed case as the training and sales evidence for next summer.

title: Fall Response Network for Meteorite Hunters
one_liner: Rapid strewn-field prediction plus standard landowner-permission contracts and a fresh-fall sales channel for meteorite hunters, extendable to satellite-debris reentries.
customer: Serious hunters and dealers (subscription), landowners and park districts (permission desks), and buyers of fresh-fall specimens.
problem: The 17 March 2026 Ohio fall drew swarms of hunters, with pieces going for roughly $400-500 per gram early on, while a golf club closed its property and a park district warned hunters off. Permission takes days, fresh-fall value decays fast, and there is no standard revenue share with landowners.
solution: Alerts within 30-60 minutes combining public bolide and radar data with hobby camera networks and automated strewn maps. A pre-registered hunter roster with waivers, a standard landowner-share contract signed digitally, on-site chain of custody, classification via a partner lab, and consignment to dealers and museums.
why_now: The Ohio fall made the economics and the access conflict public. Open satellite and radar data and cheap all-sky cameras exist, and Starlink reentries add a second, insurer-relevant use case.
revenue_model: $20/month alerts, 10-15% of specimen sales, landowner-desk fees from park districts and insurers, and data licensing.
non_obvious_insight: Strewn-field maps are already published free, so the scarce thing is access and legitimacy in the first 72 hours. A contract-and-permission layer turns hostile landowners into revenue partners and creates an exclusive right-of-entry that cannot be scraped.
first_30_days: Build a 200-person hunter Discord and draft a standard landowner agreement. Test it on the next reported fireball with 20 landowners, and sign 2 dealers to buy through the network.

title: Compute-Heated Pools and Saunas
one_liner: Install small immersion-cooled compute clusters in municipal pools, Ys and recovery studios so the servers pay for the heat.
customer: Municipal pools, YMCAs and hotels with heavy heating bills, recovery studios with saunas, and the AI batch-inference buyers who rent the compute.
problem: Pools and sauna rooms are among the largest energy line items in public and wellness facilities and many public pools are cut when budgets tighten, while AI compute needs cooling and dumps its waste heat.
solution: Deploy a 20-50 kW 'digital boiler' in the plant room that heats pool or sauna water through a heat exchanger, sell the compute to latency-tolerant inference or batch customers, and give the facility free or discounted heat. First product: a single-site pilot funded by a state energy grant and reserved compute.
why_now: A UK pilot at Exmouth Leisure Centre (a 28 kW cluster) reportedly cut the pool's gas use by 62 percent and saved about 24,000 dollars a year while the operator paid for the electricity; AI compute scarcity and edge inference demand are high in 2026 and decarbonization grants are available.
revenue_model: Compute revenue shared with the host, monthly heat fee or discount, and grants; gross margin from selling the heat.
non_obvious_insight: Both sides get paid: the compute buyer gets free cooling and the pool gets free heat, and a pool is a 24/7 constant heat sink unlike offices. The real customer is the compute buyer, with pools as cheap distributed real estate. Capital needs are real, so lead with a grant-funded pilot.
first_30_days: Find a gas-heated pool operator and a champion on the board, sign an MOU, commission a 10-20 kW pilot design with an immersion-cooling vendor, apply to two energy grant programs, and pre-sell reserved compute to two batch-inference customers.

title: Scam Recovery Desk for Community Banks
one_liner: Banks buy scam detection, but the untapped money is recovery: stablecoin issuers, receiving banks and exchanges can freeze funds if someone asks fast and correctly.
customer: Community banks and credit unions ($500M-$10B assets) that increasingly eat scam reimbursements. American Banker (2026-07-22) puts bank-side scam losses at $68B, against the FTC's $15.9B of consumer-reported losses.
problem: A community bank's fraud analyst has hours before funds move on. They don't know who to call at receiving banks, exchanges or issuer compliance desks. They have no standard evidence pack, so recoveries run to a few percent and losses are written off as a cost of doing business.
solution: A 24/7 recovery desk plus software. When a victim reports a scam, the desk traces the funds (wire, Zelle and ACH recall, plus on-chain tracing for crypto off-ramps). It sends recall, 314(b) and law-enforcement freeze requests with pre-validated evidence packs to a maintained directory of receiving-institution and issuer contacts, then tracks outcomes. The desk is paid a share of every dollar recovered.
why_now: FTC losses hit a record $15.9B in 2025, and scam flows increasingly touch stablecoins. The Senate Democrats' Tether report (2026-09-28) raises pressure on issuers to respond quickly, and GENIUS-era issuers must be able to honor lawful freeze orders (verify exact text).
revenue_model: 15-25% contingency on recovered funds plus a flat monthly retainer for 24/7 coverage.
non_obvious_insight: Recovery rates depend on speed and relationships, not analytics, so a maintained contact directory and playbook is an operations moat. Stablecoins are counterintuitively the most freezable scam rail, more so than wires or Zelle, if you know the freeze path.
first_30_days: Offer five community banks a free post-mortem of their last 90 days of scam cases and estimate the recoverable share. Hire two ex-bank fraud investigators. Sign two contingency pilots and build the first version of the issuer and receiving-bank contact directory.

title: Timed Slots for Viral Fields and Harvest Rescue
one_liner: Ticketing built around bloom and ripeness windows that turns crop-trampling influencers and crew-short fields into capped, paid visitor days.
customer: Specialty and mid-size growers with photogenic or U-pick crops near metros (tulips, lavender, sunflowers, blueberries, peaches, apples, pumpkins), especially those with unharvested acres from crew shortages. Rural tourism boards are a second payer.
problem: Viral fields get trampled while farmers earn nothing, and destinations lack allocation tools (Fuji's hard cap is the model). Meanwhile fruit rotted in fields in 2025 for lack of pickers and late or absent H-2A crews mean lost revenue. Farms squeezed by diesel up 80% and a fourth loss-making row-crop year need any extra income.
solution: Bloom and ripeness forecasts from degree-day models and owner photos drive timed-entry capacity by field zone, waivers, weigh-station POS for pay-per-pound U-pick, and parking and shuttle management. A 'harvest rescue weekend' feature lets a farm that is short of pickers list a paid visitor-harvest event 5-10 days out, with dynamic pricing by forecast and weather. Dispersal nudges route overflow to lesser-known partner farms, and nearby motel beds can be bundled.
why_now: Crew shortages, high input costs and social-media virality are all at peak in 2026, and destinations from Barcelona to Glasgow are moving from fees to allocation. Agritourism liability laws are widespread. Lead times are shortening to about 33 days, so last-minute local trips are growing.
revenue_model: 8-12% of ticket value plus $1.50-$2.50 per ticket in payments. $199/season SaaS for farms. Sponsored dispersal campaigns from tourism boards.
non_obvious_insight: A crop calendar is a supply curve with a 7-14 day peak, so the same forecast tells a farmer when to harvest and a tourist when to come. One dataset prices both the labour gap and the crowd, and U-pick as an emergency labour substitute is a hedge farms already improvise but nobody productises.
first_30_days: Sign 5 orchards and pumpkin farms for immediate October weekend slots to test capacity caps and pricing this month. Then sign 10 farms for spring 2027 tulips and strawberries starting in January, using white-label Stripe ticket pages before building custom software.

title: On-Demand Human Witnesses for Scrap and Recycled Claims
angle: Pairing 1: AI labor-market disruption x waste/circular economy/critical minerals
one_liner: A network of trained, insured, credentialed ex-auditors and QA people who can be dispatched within 24 hours to physically inspect scrap lots and witness recycled-content claims, producing tamper-evident signed reports.
customer: Remote buyers of bales and scrap lots (PET reclaimers, black-mass and tungsten buyers, brokers, traders). Brands making recycled-content claims, and their insurers and lenders. The buyers' own AI purchasing agents consume the reports through an API.
problem: PET bales trade at a record-low 1.44 c/lb while food-grade supply is called constrained, which points to a quality-tier mismatch nobody can see without inspection. Generative AI makes photos, scale tickets and certificates trivially forgeable. Traditional inspectors have minimum fees and multi-day lead times. Mass-balance claims are contested and no standard exists. California's AB 2253 (claim substantiation) was vetoed, leaving brands exposed to litigation. EU rules banning generic green claims (Directive 2024/825) began applying on Sept 27, 2026.
solution: Recruit displaced auditors, QA analysts, supply-chain and compliance staff and give them a one-day protocol course on bale and scrap specs. Dispatch them to open and grade bales, XRF-screen metals, seal loads, witness weigh-outs and attend recycled-content production runs. They use a capture app with device attestation and signed provenance, and every report is machine-readable. Visits cost $95-250 versus $800+ for traditional inspection. Each witness builds a portable, scored reputation, so the credential becomes their asset.
why_now: AI forgery capability is now cheap and widely known, so document trust is falling. The BIS Aug 27 rule adds recordkeeping for black mass and tungsten scrap. Brands need substantiation now that the EU rules apply. Agentic procurement needs verifiable physical inputs. The supply of trained auditors and analysts is growing because of AI-driven cuts.
revenue_model: Per-inspection fee split about 60/40 with the witness. Monthly claim-assurance subscriptions for brands ($1-3K). API and report-verification fees for buyers' agents. Later, a quality-tier index of bales sold to the market.
non_obvious_insight: When AI can fake any document, the scarce commodity is a credentialed human who was physically present. The scrap trade runs on thin margins and unverifiable quality claims, so cheap, fast human presence beats expensive certification. AI displacement supplies the witnesses at the same moment it destroys trust in paperwork.
first_30_days: Pick one corridor with several bale or e-scrap buyers and offer 20 discounted bale inspections to three remote buyers. Recruit and train 10 witnesses (ex-QA and audit). Build the capture flow on existing attestation and C2PA tools. Publish a first bale-quality report from the results.

title: Flood Closing Desk for Title Agents
one_liner: A day-one flood file on every purchase: elevation, zone challenge, private flood substitute and NFIP-lapse fallback.
customer: Title and escrow agencies and mortgage brokers in coastal and riverine markets, with contingency fees from homeowners.
problem: NFIP authority expires Sept 30 2026 after more than 30 short-term extensions. In the 2010 lapse about 1,400 closings a day were delayed or cancelled (secondary source). Even without a lapse, zone and elevation problems surface on day 25 of a 30-day contract, and premiums must roughly double toward full risk.
solution: An order-time 'Flood File': LiDAR-derived elevation, zone confirmation, candidates for a Letter of Map Amendment, an instant private-flood quote with a compliance letter as an NFIP substitute during lapses, and a Risk Rating 2.0 estimate. Title agencies embed it in their order flow.
why_now: Authority lapses in two days, and premium glide-path increases make every flood file a live cost.
revenue_model: $95-250 per file, $500-1,500 contingency for successful zone removal, and private flood placement commission.
non_obvious_insight: Buyers and lenders pay to avoid closing delays. Zone challenges are an arbitrage, since a successful removal saves the owner premiums every year.
first_30_days: Contract with 5 title offices, partner with a surveyor, hand-deliver 100 files, and track removal success rates.

title: Data Act Access-Request Desk for Independent Repairers
one_liner: A clearinghouse that files, tracks and escalates EU Data Act data-access requests to connected-product makers on behalf of independent garages, installers and fleet operators.
customer: Independent repair-shop networks, heat-pump and solar installers, agricultural-machinery service firms and small fleet operators (10-500 vehicles or machines) in the EU, plus their trade associations.
problem: Connected products must give users direct data access by design from 12 Sep 2026, and users can direct sharing to third parties. Every manufacturer will build its own portal, format and terms, and has every incentive to slow-walk independents. The EU repair directive transposition deadline (31 Jul 2026) also just passed. Small firms know wrenches, not statutory request letters or how to reach a national competent authority.
solution: A standardized request generator, a directory of each manufacturer's access method, a tracker with statutory-timeline reminders, normalization of the most-wanted data (fault codes, usage, battery health) and an escalation pack for the national authority. Launch with five manufacturers in two product categories.
why_now: The Data Act design obligation date was 12 Sep 2026, the repair directive deadline was 31 Jul 2026 and the EU repair platform is due 1 Jan 2028. Independents just received rights with no plumbing.
revenue_model: $49-149/month per shop, $5-20 per vehicle or machine per year for fleets, association licenses, and paid negotiation of bulk access terms.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance startups sell to the obligated party. The Data Act creates a beneficiary class that is fragmented and unsophisticated about law. The AirHelp pattern applies: rights that are costly to file individually but cheap to file collectively.
first_30_days: Sign two trade associations (independent aftermarket or agricultural repair). Send 20 manual requests across five OEMs and log response times, then publish an 'OEM Data Act responsiveness scorecard' to earn press and members. Charge $99/month.

title: Arc-Flash and Protection Studies Factory
one_liner: Deliver PE-stamped short-circuit, coordination and arc-flash studies in days rather than months, using AI to turn photos and one-lines into models.
customer: Electrical contractors and EPCs building C&I storage, EV depots and data center electrical rooms, plus facility managers facing five-year label refreshes.
problem: Power-systems engineers are scarce and studies gate energization and permits, with 8-12 week backlogs. A delayed 60 MW site costs about $3M a week. NFPA 70E requires reassessment every five years, and small C&I storage projects cannot afford $30k custom studies.
solution: Studies as a productized service. The contractor uploads single-line diagrams, nameplate photos and the utility fault-current letter. AI extracts the equipment and builds the ETAP or SKM model, a licensed PE reviews and stamps it, and the customer gets labels and coordination settings on a five-business-day SLA at a flat price per switchboard.
why_now: Vision and language models now parse one-lines and nameplates well enough to draft models. The data center and storage boom, and the engineer shortage, make throughput the scarce resource.
revenue_model: $3-15k per small C&I study, $30-100k per data center study, and recurring five-year renewals plus label printing.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody lacks software. They lack stamps and turnaround time. PE-supervised throughput with AI drafts is a labor arbitrage that stays unglamorous enough to avoid heavy competition.
first_30_days: Recruit two retired power-systems PEs. Build the extraction pipeline on 20 anonymized one-lines. Sell five C&I storage installers a $4k fixed-price study with a five-day SLA. Measure margins.

title: Carrier Watchtower: Insurer Failure Alerts for Lenders
one_liner: Early-warning scores on the thinly capitalized insurers behind mortgage collateral, sold to servicers before the next carrier failure.
customer: Mortgage subservicers, credit unions, community banks and MSR investors with Florida, Louisiana, California and Texas collateral.
problem: Insiders treat Florida as fixed because Citizens fell from 936K to about 395K policies. But take-out carriers got Citizens' data to cherry-pick policies. A CBS investigation (unverified detail) alleges owners of a receiving carrier diverted millions. Howden warns reinsurer returns may fall below cost of capital by 2027, so any reversal hits the retail layer first. If a carrier fails, thousands of loans lose hazard cover at once and servicers must force-place at multiples.
solution: Loan tape in, exposure out. Map each loan's insurer from insurance-tracking data to a live stress score built from statutory filings, reinsurance program renewals, assumed-policy concentration, complaint ratios, rating actions and regulator orders. Give a 90-day warning and a pre-negotiated replacement placement lane.
why_now: Florida's rapid depopulation of Citizens in 2025-26 moved risk onto newer, thinner balance sheets. Reinsurance is at record capital and softening now, and the margin squeeze is forecast for 2027.
revenue_model: SaaS priced at basis points or cents per loan per year, plus per-policy replacement placement fees.
non_obvious_insight: Analysts watch carrier surplus and lenders watch loans, but nobody joins the two. Rating agencies lag, and the soft market hides the fragility.
first_30_days: Build dossiers on the top 40 Florida carriers from public regulator filings. Sell a $5K exposure report to two credit unions or subservicers showing what share of their book sits with the weakest carriers.

title: Pre-Permitted Gateway Campuses for Satellite Constellations
one_liner: A real-estate developer for multi-tenant satellite gateway sites with power, fiber, interference studies and landing-right support.
customer: Constellation operators (broadband, direct-to-cell, EO downlink) that need dozens of gateways in many countries, and ground-station-as-a-service providers.
problem: Every constellation needs gateways that are radio-quiet, low in rain fade, and connected to fiber and power. Zoning, community opposition and national landing rights make site acquisition slow, and launching more satellites does not help if gateways are the bottleneck. AST is launch-constrained now, but ground capacity is next.
solution: Option, entitle and pre-permit 'gateway campuses' in strategic regions, then lease antenna pads on 10-15 year terms. Include interference and rain-fade studies, fiber and power, and local licensing help. Start in the Caribbean, Latin America and Africa, where landing rights and site scarcity bind hardest.
why_now: Launch capacity is exploding, so the bottleneck shifts to the ground. Spectrum is now owned by operators with big plans (SpaceX, AT&T, AST). Direct-to-cell needs many gateways to reach many carriers.
revenue_model: Pad leases $8-25k per month per antenna. Development fee on entitlement assignment. Long-term power and fiber pass-through margin.
non_obvious_insight: Operators over-invest in satellites and under-invest in the boring ground sites that gate capacity. Zoning boards, not rockets, may be the binding constraint.
first_30_days: Use GIS to shortlist 30 parcels near fiber and power across five regions. Take low-cost options on five. Get LOIs from two gateway-hungry operators or teleport providers before spending on entitlements.

title: Paid Caregiver Demonstration-Data Cooperative
angle: Pairing 1: Aging/silver economy x Logistics & physical automation
one_liner: Home-care aides and family caregivers wear head cameras during non-intimate care tasks and earn revenue share from licensing that data to robot-foundation-model companies.
customer: Robotics labs and humanoid makers buying home-task demonstration data (Figure, 1X, Skild, Physical Intelligence, Generalist-class buyers), at $60-150 per usable hour. Home-care agencies are the distribution partner.
problem: Humanoid progress is bottlenecked on physical-world data. Data vendors already pay people to film themselves making coffee (XDOF about $50M annualized, Mecka projecting $100M ARR). Nobody has data on the hardest, highest-value home tasks: walker and transfer assistance, modified-diet meal prep, laundry and tidying around frail people. Meanwhile aides earn under $35k and agencies see 77-80% turnover.
solution: Give each aide a $150 camera kit and an on-device consent and blurring pipeline. Capture only task categories that avoid intimate care, with care-recipient or proxy consent per home. Pay a per-hour data premium on top of wages, which agencies use as a retention bonus, and sell curated, labeled datasets.
why_now: Robot data-as-a-service went from nothing to unicorn valuations in months (Sep 2026). Immigration crackdowns are draining the care workforce, so agencies are desperate for retention tools that do not raise Medicaid-capped rates.
revenue_model: License datasets at $60-150 per hour. Pay workers 30-40%, agency 10% and keep the remainder. Add curation and labeling fees.
non_obvious_insight: Robots cannot yet enter the homes that hold the training data they most need, but the lowest-paid workforce in America is already inside them. Data pay solves agencies' turnover problem at no cost to a squeezed Medicaid budget.
first_30_days: Sign one home-care agency and 20 aides for a pilot. Write a consent and privacy protocol with an elder-law attorney. Pre-sell a 500-hour dataset to one robotics lab using a sample of kitchen and laundry tasks.

title: Training-Day School Inside Youth Sports Facilities
one_liner: Turn the empty weekday hours of club-sports facilities into ESA- and scholarship-funded microschools for serious young athletes.
customer: Owners of independent indoor youth-sports facilities (volleyball, gymnastics, basketball, hockey, tennis/pickleball, swim) in ESA and voucher states such as AZ, FL, TX and UT. Tuition is paid by families out of ESA, voucher or (from 2027) scholarship-granting-organization funds.
problem: Facilities carry rent and HVAC costs but sit idle roughly 8am-3pm on weekdays, because their revenue is concentrated in evenings and weekends. Families spending thousands a year on club sports fight school schedules, travel and early mornings. Microschool compliance (registration, occupancy, insurance, ESA vendor status) is daunting for a gym owner. School status also matters financially: in Texas, registered private-school kids get about $10,474 in ESA money while homeschoolers get about $2,000.
solution: A turnkey 'training-day school' kit. It includes state-specific school registration and a change-of-occupancy checklist, a low-screen paper-based mastery curriculum from a partner, hiring and training of a credentialed lead teacher plus coach-guides, insurance, ESA/SGO vendor enrollment and tuition billing. The daily schedule is 3 hours of academics plus 3 hours of training. Opt-in wearable sleep and load data decides when the hard academic blocks and the hard training blocks fall. The facility fills 20-40 seats at ESA-level tuition during dead hours.
why_now: ESA money is scaling (Texas had 200k+ applicants). The federal $1,700 scholarship tax credit starts in 2027 with 31 states opted in, yet about 1,000 microschools are in limbo awaiting Treasury rules, so operators want ready-made compliance. Alpha School (about 50 campuses, heart-rate monitors) has shown parents will pay for short academics plus afternoon workshops. 61% of teachers now want less device use, and homeschooling is transient (about 30% do it for 1-2 years), so hybrid products fit.
revenue_model: $12-20k setup fee per facility plus 8-10% of tuition, or $1.5k/month SaaS plus billing fees. A site with 25 students at $8-10k is about $200-250k of tuition a year, so roughly $20k a year recurring to us per site. Add referral fees on curriculum and insurance.
non_obvious_insight: Alpha School sells a schedule, not a building. The scarcest inputs (a big safe space, coaches, motivated kids, parents with athletic budgets) already exist in every metro at sports facilities that lose money on weekdays. Boarding sports academies cost $70k+; the mid-market, ESA-priced version does not exist yet, and the gating constraint is building code, so the wedge is a compliance kit for the friendliest states.
first_30_days: Pick one state with microschool-friendly occupancy rules (for example Arizona or Florida). Contact 40 facility owners through club-owner groups and facility trade associations and sign 2-3 letters of intent. Pre-enroll 10-15 athlete families with $500 deposits for a January semester. Hire a part-time certified teacher as head of school, and use an existing curriculum partner plus a lawyer-reviewed compliance template.

title: Courthouse-Handwriting Graph to Clear Heirs' Property
one_liner: Use AI that can read old handwritten deeds and probate files to map who really owns family land that never went through probate, and sell clean title to the buyers who need it.
customer: Solar, wind, pipeline and broadband developers, land trusts and conservation buyers, timber and ag buyers, and title insurers, with legal-aid partners protecting heirs.
problem: When a landowner dies without probate, title fragments among dozens of heirs. Developers can't lease or buy without consent, and heirs can lose land through partition sales. The records are handwritten across probate, deed and marriage files, so clearing one parcel takes lawyers weeks or months.
solution: LLM handwriting recognition over courthouse records builds a family-of-record graph per parcel, ranks probable heirs, finds them, and manages consent, lease or purchase packages through e-signature. Partner attorneys file quiet-title or partition actions for hard cases. Developers get a 'title-readiness score' per parcel. The design bakes in fair terms and legal aid for heirs.
why_now: Multimodal models now read historical cursive at near-human accuracy, and county records are increasingly scanned. The Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act has been adopted in a couple dozen states, which pushes toward consensual deals. The land rush for solar and data-center sites needs clean title fast.
revenue_model: $2K-$10K per cleared parcel paid by the developer or a percentage of lease value, plus data licensing to title insurers.
non_obvious_insight: The transfer that never went through probate, family land passed informally for generations, is a hidden inventory of blocked assets. Now a buyer with money (energy and data infrastructure) will pay to clear it.
first_30_days: Pick one county in a solar-active area with high heirs' property prevalence. Get a developer's list of blocked parcels. Process 10 parcels and partner with a heirs' property legal clinic to review the process and heir outreach.

title: Rescue Monitoring for Orphaned Home Solar
one_liner: An installer-agnostic gateway plus subscription that watches home solar systems whose installer went bankrupt, produces warranty-ready evidence, and dispatches a vetted local electrician.
customer: Homeowners with installer-abandoned solar systems (owned or financed). B2B: solar loan servicers and asset managers holding loans and leases from failed installers, who care about collateral performance. Local electricians and solar technicians are the fulfillment network.
problem: Installers such as Sunnova (Chapter 11 in June 2025, roughly 500,000 customers) and others collapsed. Systems keep running, but nobody is watching or servicing them. Silent faults (failed optimizers, tripped rapid shutdown, inverter errors) can cost months of production. Warranty claims require documentation the homeowner doesn't have, and installer apps degrade or vanish.
solution: A gateway that reads inverter data locally (SunSpec Modbus and local APIs) plus a CT clamp on the main panel. It compares actual output to modeled output using open weather and irradiance data, classifies probable fault types (string, inverter, shading, curtailment), and generates a warranty evidence pack for the equipment manufacturers. A flat-fee price sheet dispatches vetted local technicians. Start with the three or four most common inverter families.
why_now: The installer failure wave (SunPower in 2024, Sunnova in 2025, many smaller firms) is producing large orphaned fleets. The federal residential solar tax credit ended for expenditures after 2025, so more installers will exit and fewer new ones will absorb the orphans. Gateways and cloud analytics are now cheap.
revenue_model: USD 8-12 per month plus a USD 150-250 gateway or a USD 199 'solar health check plus 12 months' bundle. Dispatch margin of 15-20% on repairs. B2B data-and-triage feed of USD 2-4 per system per month for servicers with 10k+ systems.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing isn't data, because the inverter clouds still exist. It's someone accountable who reads the data and moves a truck. Sell a primary-care doctor for a solar system with a referral network. Lenders care because a non-producing system correlates with default, which gives a second payer.
first_30_days: Recruit orphan-solar homeowners through r/solar and Facebook groups. Ship 50 gateways to owners of two or three inverter families. Sign 3-5 electricians in Texas, California, Arizona or Florida on a fixed price sheet. Sell the health-check bundle and use the first detected faults as marketing proof. Approach two loan servicers with the aggregate underperformance findings.

title: Flat-Fee Guarantee Against Runaway Agent Bills
one_liner: Pay a few percent on top of model spend and the guarantee absorbs any overnight blowout above a hard multiple of baseline, enforced by an inline kill switch.
customer: AI-native startups and agencies spending $5k-$200k per month on model and tool calls (seed to Series B), including dev shops deploying agents for clients.
problem: Retry loops turn $0.40 tasks into $40, and five-figure overnight bills are reported. Blended token prices fell about 67% in a year but agentic workflows burn 5-30x more tokens, and 73% of enterprises overran AI budgets. The market sells dashboards and caps. Nobody sells a promise, and founders and their investors want the tail risk gone.
solution: A drop-in proxy (change one base URL) that sees all model and tool traffic and learns a rolling baseline per agent and workflow. The guarantee covers spend above a set multiple of baseline in a rolling window (for example 4x over 6 hours), up to a cap, paid as cash or credits. The proxy enforces circuit breakers so maximum loss is bounded, which makes underwriting tractable. Coverage applies only where default breaker policies were accepted, which controls moral hazard.
why_now: TechCrunch was covering the scramble over runaway AI costs by June 2026. Gateways are being absorbed into security suites (Palo Alto bought Portkey), and dozens of cap-and-alert tools have commoditized enforcement without offering a guarantee.
revenue_model: 3-6% premium on metered spend plus a gateway subscription, with parametric or MGA reinsurance for large limits.
non_obvious_insight: Whoever owns the kill switch can price the tail. A capped, enforced exposure is a parametric insurance product, not an open-ended liability. Buyers are paying for certainty, and the tooling is only how you deliver it.
first_30_days: Ship an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible proxy with breakers. Sign 10 startups to a beta guarantee capped at about $2k per incident, backed by a roughly $20k reserve. Price at about 4% of spend and log every incident. Talk to two parametric or MGA capacity providers.

title: Bridge Loans for Medicare Drug-Price Refunds
one_liner: Fund the 3-4 week float independent pharmacies now carry on Medicare's negotiated-price drugs, underwritten on predictable refund data, before Ozempic joins the list in January.
customer: Independent pharmacies with senior-heavy books, especially those serving long-term care, then 5-50 store groups and PSAOs. Average exposure is estimated at over $27,000 a month per community pharmacy.
problem: Since January 1, 2026, pharmacies pay wholesalers full price for Eliquis, Jardiance, Xarelto, Farxiga, Januvia, Entresto and others, dispense at Medicare's Maximum Fair Price, and wait weeks for the difference to arrive through the Medicare Transaction Facilitator. Estimates put the float at $27k+ a month for the average community pharmacy, over $500M a month industry-wide, on top of wholesalers who still auto-debit weekly. On thin margins that is a real solvency risk. Banks see a pharmacy, not an insured refund.
solution: Start with a reconciliation tool that ingests the pharmacy's PMS claims export and the MTF remittance files and shows late or missing refunds. Then offer a non-recourse advance of about 90% of the expected refund on each week's MFP claims, repaid from the actual MTF payment through a controlled deposit account or sweep. Confirm with CMS and the facilitator what payment-routing options exist, and fall back to a bank-account sweep if third-party routing is not allowed.
why_now: The program only became real on January 1, 2026, and it is already causing cash-flow warnings from pharmacy coalitions. On January 1, 2027, 15 more drugs join, including semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus), which multiplies the float. Wholesalers have not yet solved it and the bank market does not understand it, so there is a window of a few quarters before someone standardizes the answer.
revenue_model: A fee of about 1-1.75% per advance cycle, which works out to roughly 15-25% annualized, plus a $99 a month reconciliation subscription. Contingency of about 10% on missing refunds recovered. Later, sell or syndicate the receivables to a credit fund.
non_obvious_insight: To a bank this looks like distress lending to a struggling small business. In reality it is close to prime paper: the obligor is a drug manufacturer with a statutory duty to pay, routed through a federal facilitator, backed by claim-level data. Only someone who knows how PMS claims map to MFP eligibility, and how a reversal or dispute can claw a refund back, can underwrite it. The free reconciliation report is the wedge that gets the data before any money goes out.
first_30_days: Offer a free 'find my missing refunds' report to 25 pharmacies through state association newsletters and pharmacy owner Facebook groups. Line up a $500k credit line from a regional bank or family office and keep the first ten advances small. Talk to a fintech attorney about commercial-financing disclosure laws by state. Approach one PSAO about distribution.
